6	import Mathlib

9	/-! # The Jacobian of a smooth proper curve
10	
11	The Jacobian of a smooth, proper, geometrically irreducible curve over a field, equipped with
12	its structure as an abelian variety.
13	
14	## Status
15	
16	The Jacobian is defined uniformly as the underlying scheme of an Albanese witness
17	(`JacobianWitness`) for the curve `C`; the four protected instances on `Jacobian C` all
18	project from the witness directly.
19	
20	The construction is **uniform in the genus**: the witness is the Picard identity
21	component `Pic⁰_{C/k}` (`picardJacobianWitness`), an abelian variety of dimension
22	`genus C` built by the FGA route (`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.*` +
23	`AlgebraicJacobian.Albanese.*`). There is **no** genus `= 0` / genus `> 0` split: when
24	`genus C = 0` the tangent space `H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` is `0`-dimensional, so `Pic⁰_{C/k} = Spec k`
25	falls out automatically. The former separate `genusZeroWitness` lane (with its
26	`RigidityKbar` / cotangent-vanishing / Frobenius / `ℙ¹`-identification machinery) was a
27	pre-FGA local optimisation and has been removed.
28	
29	This file contains exactly ONE `sorry`-bodied mathematical declaration,
30	`picardJacobianWitness`, whose closure is the FGA construction of `Pic⁰_{C/k}` as an
31	abelian variety with its Albanese universal property.
32	
33	The file contains:
34	- `IsAlbanese`: the Albanese universal property for a pointed curve.
35	- `IsAlbanese.unique`: uniqueness of the Albanese object up to canonical isomorphism.
36	- `JacobianWitness`: a bundled candidate Albanese object together with the universal
37	  property uniformly over the choice of $k$-rational marked point.
38	- `picardJacobianWitness`: the Albanese witness `J = Pic⁰_{C/k}`, body `sorry`.
39	- `nonempty_jacobianWitness`: existence of an Albanese witness for every curve,
40	  delegating to `picardJacobianWitness`.
41	- `Jacobian` and its four protected instances, each obtained by projection from the
42	  Albanese witness.
43	
44	### Forbidden shortcut (sanity check)
45	
46	Defining `Jacobian C := 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k)))` *unconditionally* (the terminal object,
47	i.e. `Spec k`) compiles and discharges three of the four instances for free, but the
48	fourth instance `SmoothOfRelativeDimension (genus C) (𝟙_ _).hom` would force `genus C = 0`,
49	which is mathematically wrong for any curve of genus `≥ 1`. The terminal-object definition
50	is therefore forbidden when `genus C > 0`. The witness-based definition avoids this
51	issue: the witness's `J` is `Pic⁰_{C/k}`, which is `Spec k` exactly when `genus C = 0`
52	and the honest Albanese object otherwise.
53	-/

77	      ∃! (g : J ⟶ A), f = α ≫ g

108	  have ⟨g, hg_eq, hg_unique⟩ := h₁.exists_unique_ofCurve_comp h₂.ofCurve h₂.comp_ofCurve

115	    refine hg₁_unique (g ≫ h) ?_
116	    change h₁.ofCurve = h₁.ofCurve ≫ (g ≫ h)
117	    rw [← Category.assoc, ← hg_eq, ← hh_eq]
118	  have hgh : g ≫ h = 𝟙 J₁ := by rw [ggh_eq_g₁, g₁_eq_id]
119	  have ⟨k₂, hk₂_eq, hk₂_unique⟩ := h₂.exists_unique_ofCurve_comp h₂.ofCurve h₂.comp_ofCurve
120	  have k₂_eq_id : k₂ = 𝟙 J₂ := by
121	    refine (hk₂_unique (𝟙 J₂) ?_).symm
122	    simp
123	  have hhg_eq_k₂ : h ≫ g = k₂ := by
124	    refine hk₂_unique (h ≫ g) ?_
125	    change h₂.ofCurve = h₂.ofCurve ≫ (h ≫ g)
126	    rw [← Category.assoc, ← hh_eq, ← hg_eq]
127	  have hhg : h ≫ g = 𝟙 J₂ := by rw [hhg_eq_k₂, k₂_eq_id]
128	  exact ⟨g, hg_eq, fun g' hg' => hg_unique g' hg'⟩

130	end IsAlbanese
131	
132	/-- A bundled Albanese witness for the smooth proper geometrically irreducible curve
133	`C`: a candidate group scheme `J` (with proper, smooth, geometrically irreducible
134	structure, smooth of relative dimension `genus C`), and a proof that `J` satisfies
135	the Albanese universal property of Definition `IsAlbanese` for `C` *for every choice
136	of $k$-rational marked point* `P : 𝟙_ _ ⟶ C`.
137	
138	Mathematically, the underlying scheme `J` (and its group/proper/smooth/irreducible
139	structure) is intrinsic to `C`; only the universal morphism `C ⟶ J` depends on the
140	choice of marked point `P`. Encoding `isAlbaneseFor` as a `∀ P, IsAlbanese …` field
141	keeps the bundle independent of any specific pointing, which is what
142	`AbelJacobi.Jacobian.ofCurve P` needs in order to project the Albanese morphism for
143	an *arbitrary* input `P`.
144	
145	The smoothness witness is recorded at the specific relative dimension `genus C`,
146	which is the form required by `Jacobian.smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus`. -/
147	structure JacobianWitness (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
148	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] where
149	  /-- The candidate Albanese object. -/
150	  J : Over (Spec (.of k))
151	  /-- The group-scheme structure on `J`. -/
152	  grpObj : GrpObj J
153	  /-- `J` is proper over `k`. -/
154	  proper : IsProper J.hom
155	  /-- `J` is smooth over `k`. -/
156	  smooth : Smooth J.hom
157	  /-- `J` is geometrically irreducible over `k`. -/
158	  geomIrred : GeometricallyIrreducible J.hom
159	  /-- `J` is smooth of relative dimension `genus C` (so dim `J = genus C`). -/
160	  smoothGenus : SmoothOfRelativeDimension (genus C) J.hom
161	  /-- The Albanese universal-property data: for every choice of $k$-rational marked
162	  point `P : 𝟙_ _ ⟶ C`, the scheme `J` together with its group/proper/smooth/irreducible
163	  structure satisfies the Albanese universal property for the pointed curve `(C, P)`. -/
164	  isAlbaneseFor : ∀ (P : 𝟙_ _ ⟶ C), @IsAlbanese k _ C P J grpObj proper smooth geomIrred
165	
166	
167	/-- The Albanese witness for a smooth proper geometrically irreducible curve `C`,
168	constructed **uniformly in the genus** as the identity component `Pic⁰_{C/k}` of the
169	Picard scheme of `C`.
170	
171	By the FGA route (`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.*`), `Pic⁰_{C/k}` is representable
172	(`Scheme.PicScheme.representable`) and is an abelian variety of dimension `genus C`:
173	its tangent space at the identity is `H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` (`Scheme.Pic0.tangentSpaceIso`),
174	giving smoothness of relative dimension `genus C` (`Scheme.Pic0.smooth`), properness
175	(`Scheme.Pic0.proper`), and geometric irreducibility
176	(`Scheme.Pic0.geometricallyIrreducible`); the Albanese universal property is the
177	Abel–Jacobi factorisation of `AlgebraicJacobian.Albanese.AlbaneseUP`.
178	
179	The genus-`0` case is **not** special and needs no separate construction: when
180	`genus C = 0` the tangent space is `0`-dimensional, so `Pic⁰_{C/k} = Spec k`
181	automatically, and the universal property degenerates to the (then trivial) statement
182	that every pointed morphism `C ⟶ A` into an abelian variety is constant. The former
183	`genusZeroWitness` / `positiveGenusWitness` genus split — together with its bespoke

11	# Representability of the Quot scheme (honest statement)
12	
13	The endgame statement of the A.2.b Quot-scheme chapter
14	(`thm:quot_representable`, [Nitsure] §5 "Main Existence Theorems"): for a
15	projective morphism `π : X ⟶ S` over a locally noetherian base, carrying a
16	relatively very ample line bundle `L`, and a coherent sheaf `E`, the Quot
17	functor `Quot^{Φ,L}_{E/X/S}` (`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.QuotFunctor`,
18	`Picard/QuotFunctorDef.lean`) is representable by an `S`-scheme.
19	
20	This file carries the **faithful restatement** settled in inbox `I-0118`:
21	projectivity of `π` with very ample `L` is encoded by
22	`Scheme.Hom.IsProjectiveWith` (`Picard/ProjectiveMorphism.lean` — a closed
23	immersion into `ℙ(Fin (d+1); S)` over `S` with `L ≅ i^* O(1)`).  The
24	statement lives here rather than in `QuotFunctorDef.lean` because the
25	projectivity vocabulary imports that file; this split mirrors
26	`Grassmannian.representable` (`GrassmannianRepresentability.lean`).
27	Everything is at `Scheme.{0}`: `IsProjectiveWith` rests on the Serre twist,
28	hence on the universe-monomorphic descent engine `Scheme.Modules.glue`
29	(`GlueDescent.lean`).
30	
31	The proof is open — the Quot endgame of [Nitsure] §5 (boundedness by
32	Castelnuovo–Mumford regularity, embedding into a relative Grassmannian,
33	flattening stratification, valuative criterion); the theorem below is its
34	single tracked `sorry`.
35	
36	Blueprint: `thm:quot_representable`
37	(`blueprint/src/chapters/Picard_QuotScheme.tex`).
38	Source: [Nitsure] §5 (FGA Explained Ch. 5, arXiv:math/0504020).

52	and `Φ ∈ ℚ[λ]`.  Then the Quot functor `Quot^{Φ,L}_{E/X/S}` is representable

9	/-!
10	# The Abel-Jacobi map
11	
12	The Abel-Jacobi map from a smooth, proper curve to its Jacobian, and the universal property
13	of the Jacobian as the Albanese variety.
14	
15	Since `Jacobian C` is by definition `(jacobianWitness C).J`, every declaration below is a
16	projection of the Albanese universal property carried by the witness field
17	`(jacobianWitness C).isAlbaneseFor P : IsAlbanese C P (jacobianWitness C).J`.
18	
19	## Main results
20	
21	* `Jacobian.ofCurve`: the Abel-Jacobi map `C ⟶ Jacobian C` attached to a `k`-rational point
22	  `P` of `C`.
23	* `Jacobian.comp_ofCurve`: the Abel-Jacobi map sends `P` to the neutral element of
24	  `Jacobian C`.
25	* `Jacobian.exists_unique_ofCurve_comp`: a morphism `f : C ⟶ A` to an abelian variety with
26	  `P ≫ f = η[A]` factors uniquely through the Abel-Jacobi map.
27	
28	## Remaining obligations
29	
30	The genus-0 rigidity input (classical rigidity `Hom(ℙ¹, A) = A(k)`) is not proved here: it is
31	part of the existence claim `nonempty_jacobianWitness` in `AlgebraicJacobian.Jacobian`, which is
32	still open.  The `isAlbaneseFor` field of a witness must verify the Albanese property for
33	genus-0 curves too, which is exactly that rigidity content.
34	
35	## References
36	
37	Source: [Mumford], *Abelian Varieties*, §4 (rigidity).
38	-/

/-!
# B3 — the rigid pushforward engine: statement layer and ℙ¹ reduction skeleton

This file pins milestone **B3** of the Picard-representability campaign
(`informal/pic-representability-campaign.md`), the engine
`pushforward_locallyFree_of_h1_vanishing`: for the constant curve
`C_A = C ×_k Spec A` over a finitely generated `k`-algebra `A` and an
invertible sheaf `L` on `C_A` with `h¹(C_t, L_t) = 0` at **every scheme
point** `t : Spec A`, the pushforward `q_* L` along `q : C_A ⟶ Spec A` is
locally free with fibre rank `h⁰(C_t, L_t) (= χ(L_t))`, and its formation
commutes with **arbitrary** ring maps `A → A'`.

Sources: Mumford, *Abelian Varieties*, II §5 (the two-term finite free
complex and "cohomology and base change"); EGA III 7.9.9; Hartshorne III
12.11; Kleiman, *The Picard scheme* (FGA Explained), §5 — B3 is the engine
behind Kleiman's flattening/openness arguments in the curve case.

## Statement audit (campaign checklist item 1 — BLOCKING; verdicts recorded here)

* **Quantifier — `h¹ = 0` at ALL scheme points** (`RigidPushforwardLocallyFree`,
  `RigidPushforwardBaseChange`): the hypothesis `∀ t : Spec A,
  q.FiberH1Vanishing L t` ranges over *all* points of the underlying space of
  `Spec A` (all primes), not only closed points.  For general noetherian `A`
  (noetherian ≠ Jacobson: e.g. a DVR, whose generic point is contained in no
  closed point's closure) the closed-point form is strictly weaker and the
  engine's conclusion FAILS if the hypothesis is checked at closed points
  only.  A finitely generated `k`-algebra *is* Jacobson, so on the pinned
  base the two forms happen to agree — but (i) the reduction uses h¹ upper
  semicontinuity, an engine we refuse to smuggle into the *statement*, and
  (ii) milestone B2 extends every consumer along filtered colimits and
  localizations, where the base is merely noetherian and Jacobson genuinely
  fails.  All campaign consumers (J1/J3 `h⁰ ≡ 1`, B4–B6) supply the
  hypothesis at all scheme points anyway.  VERDICT: pin at all scheme points.
* **Base change along ARBITRARY `A → A'` in the statement**
  (`RigidPushforwardBaseChange`): quantified over every commutative ring
  `A' : Type u` and every ring hom `φ : A →+* A'` — no finiteness, no
  flatness, no noetherian hypothesis on `A'`.  The comparison morphism is
  the canonical `pushforwardBaseChangeMap` (Stacks 02N4-style mate) of the
  *defining pullback square* of `q` along `Spec φ`, so the statement is
  well-formed with zero transport: the base-changed family is
  `pullback q (Spec.map φ)` — canonically (but not definitionally) isomorphic
  to `C ×_k Spec A'`; the comparison iso is postponed to the consumer layer
  (B2), keeping the pin transport-free.  VERDICT: arbitrary `A'`, arbitrary
  `φ`, canonical square, comparison map in the statement.
* **Two-step pin**: step 1 = rank-`χ` local freeness
  (`RigidPushforwardLocallyFree`) + base change
  (`RigidPushforwardBaseChange`); step 2 = the rank-one corollary
  (`pushforward_isLocallyTrivial_of_h1_vanishing`, proved from the gate).
  VERDICT: pinned as two separate `Prop`s consumed by one gate.
* **Rank = `χ(L_t)`** : under `h¹(L_t) = 0` we have `χ(L_t) = h⁰(L_t)`, and
  `h⁰` *is* expressible today (`Scheme.Hom.fiberH0`, the `κ(t)`-dimension of
  `Γ(C_t, L_t)`, matching `Scheme.hilbertFunction`'s convention), while the
  `χ`-ledger is milestone P3.  The rank is therefore pinned as
  `q.fiberH0 L t`; **P2/P3-interface TODO**: once the P2 cohomology kit and
  the P3 `χ`-ledger land, add the (definitionally compatible) reformulation
  `rank = χ(L_t) = deg L_t + 1 - g`.
* **Fibrewise `h¹` vocabulary** (P2 does not exist yet): the hypothesis is
  pinned in the weakest honest form the adelic lane can already express —
  existence of a 2-affine Čech cover (`AffineCoverMVSquare`, the lane's
  carrier) of the scheme-theoretic fibre on which the degree-1 Čech
  cokernel of `L_t` vanishes, i.e. the difference-of-restrictions map is
  surjective (`Scheme.Hom.FiberH1Vanishing`; carrier form
  `AffineCoverMVSquare.moduleH1Cok`, mirroring
  `AffineCoverMVSquare.H1Cok` of `RiemannRoch/Adelic/Cokernel.lean`).  On a
  separated scheme with an affine 2-cover, this Čech `H¹` computes sheaf
  `H¹` for quasi-coherent modules (Mayer–Vietoris/Leray; in-lane precedent
  `hModuleOne_linearEquiv_cechCohomology`), and any two such covers agree —
  cover-independence is exactly the **P2-interface TODO**, to be discharged
  Čech-to-Čech.  The ∃-form is chosen because it is *implied* by every
  future kit form, so the gate only gets easier to discharge.
* **The rank-one corollary's `DivFamily` leg** (Kleiman §5; campaign J2):
  `h⁰ ≡ 1, h¹ ≡ 0 ⟹ q_*L` invertible is pinned and proved from the gate
  below.  The continuation — the counit section `q^*q_*L ⟶ L` is fibrewise
  nonzero, hence a regular section on the integral fibres, hence cuts a
  canonical `DivFamily` — needs the counit/adjunction vocabulary on the
  `Div` side and the geometric integrality of fibres; it is recorded as the
  **J2-interface TODO** and deliberately NOT pinned here (its natural home
  is the J2 session, where the target `DivFamily` shape is fixed).

## Gate

`HasRigidPushforward C` is the campaign gate (`HasPicScheme` pattern): a
`Prop` class with **no instances anywhere**, carrying the two statement
`Prop`s quantified over all finitely generated `k`-algebras.  It is
discharged by the full B3 session (Mumford two-term complex route) and
deleted on discharge.  Everything else in this file is *proved*: the
extraction theorems, the rank-one corollary, and the ℙ¹ reduction skeleton
(the base-changed finite map `C_A ⟶ ℙ¹_A`, the pushforward factorization
`q_* = p_* ∘ π_*`, and the reduction of B3-for-`C_A` to a ℙ¹ engine plus a
named finite-pushforward transfer package).
-/

# B3 transfer package — discharging the named hypotheses of the ℙ¹ reduction

`Picard/RigidPushforward.lean` reduces B3 local freeness for the constant
curve `C_A` to the ℙ¹ engine plus a *finite-pushforward transfer package*
along the finite map `π_A : C_A ⟶ ℙ¹_A` (`rigidPushforwardLocallyFree_of_p1`,
hypotheses `hfp`/`hflat`/`hH1`/`hH0`).  This file discharges the first two
transfer hypotheses:

* **`hfp` (Stacks 01XZ/087T flavour)** —
  `pushforward_finiteMapToP1BaseChange_isFinitePresentation`: the finite
  pushforward `(π_A)_* L` of an invertible module is finitely presented.
  The engine behind it is the general noetherian coherence criterion
  `Scheme.Modules.isFinitePresentation_of_finite_sections`: a quasi-coherent
  module on a locally noetherian scheme whose section modules over affine
  opens are finite is finitely presented.  The pushforward is quasi-coherent
  by Stacks 01XJ (`pushforward_isQuasicoherent`, proved in
  `Picard/QuotScheme.lean`), its sections over an affine `V` are
  `Γ(L, π_A⁻¹ V)` *definitionally*, and these are module-finite over
  `Γ(ℙ¹_A, V)` by composing the module-finiteness of the finite morphism
  `π_A` (Stacks 01WG) with the finiteness of the sections of the finitely
  presented `L` on the affine `π_A⁻¹ V` (Stacks 01PC,
  `finite_sections_preimage_of_isAffineHom`).  `A` is a finitely generated
  `k`-algebra, hence noetherian (Hilbert basis), hence `ℙ¹_A` is locally
  noetherian and finite section modules are finitely presented.

* **`hflat` (mixed-base flat stability)** —
  `pushforward_finiteMapToP1BaseChange_coherentSheafFlat`: `(π_A)_* L`
  stays `CoherentSheafFlat` over `Spec A`.  Since
  `Γ((π_A)_* L, V) = Γ(L, π_A⁻¹ V)` definitionally and
  `q = π_A ≫ p` (`finiteMapToP1BaseChange_snd`), the statement reduces to
  `CoherentSheafFlat q L` for the invertible `L` on the `A`-flat family
  `q : C_A ⟶ Spec A` (`coherentSheafFlat_pushforward_of_isAffineHom`).
  The latter is `coherentSheafFlat_of_isLocallyTrivial_of_flat`: on a
  trivialising affine chart `W` the section module `Γ(L, W)` is an
  invertible (hence flat) `Γ(C_A, W)`-module
  (`isInvertible_of_restrict_iso`), `Γ(C_A, W)` is flat over `A` because
  `q` is a flat morphism (base change of `C ⟶ Spec k`, and everything over
  the one-point integral `Spec k` is flat), and chart flatness globalises
  to all affine pairs by the affine-locality engine
  `flat_section_of_affine_cover` (`Picard/GenericFlatnessGeometric.lean`).

* **transfer item (c) — the fibre-compatibility isomorphism and `hH0`**
  (§6–§7): the general Stacks 02KG (`i = 0`) engine for **affine**
  morphisms and **arbitrary** (non-flat) base change

* **`hH1`** — the cover-independence obligation `hindep` is
  discharged by the QC-vanishing keystone
  (`Cohomology/StructureSheafModuleK/QuasicoherentDegreeOneVanishing.lean`:

No pinned statement is touched: this file only *produces* the named
hypotheses consumed by `rigidPushforwardLocallyFree_of_p1`.

10	/-!
11	# FGA representability of the Picard scheme
12	
13	This file states the FGA representability of the relative Picard functor of a
14	smooth proper geometrically integral curve `C/k`, following Kleiman, "The
15	Picard scheme", §2 and §4 (cf. FGA Explained Ch. 9; arXiv:math/0504020).
16	
17	The relative Picard functor is
18	
19	```
20	picSharp C := PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⋙ forget AddCommGrpCat
21	```
22	
23	the set-valued shadow of the `H_T`-coset carrier
24	`T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)` of `Picard/RelPicFunctor.lean` (Kleiman §2
25	Def. `df:Pfs`; blueprint `def:rel_pic_sharp`). A `RepresentableBy` witness
26	against it is a natural bijection
27	`(T ⟶ Pic_{C/k}) ≃ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)`, which is what the downstream
28	tangent-space computation (`AJC.pic0av`, `Pic0.tangentSpaceIso`) attaches to.
29	
30	## The étale-sheafification route: Kleiman §2 Thm 2.5
31	
32	Kleiman §4 represents the **étale-sheafified** functor `Pic_{(C/k)ét}`.
33	Mathlib at the pinned revision has no étale Grothendieck topology on
34	schemes, so instead of sheafifying we use Kleiman §2 **Thm 2.5**: when
35	`f : X → S` has a **section** and `O_S = f_* O_X` holds universally (true
36	for our proper geometrically integral `C/k`), the comparison maps
37	
38	```
39	Pic_{X/S}(T) → Pic_{(X/S)ét}(T) → Pic_{(X/S)fppf}(T)
40	```
41	
42	are all **bijective**. Hence, under a `k`-rational-point hypothesis
43	(`HasRationalPoint C` below), the *plain* relative functor `picSharp C` is
44	itself representable, and the FGA statement can be made against it directly
45	— no étale topology needed. Without a section the plain functor is not
46	representable in general (it need not even be a Zariski sheaf), which is why
47	representability is asserted only **conditionally on `[HasRationalPoint C]`**:
48	an unconditional statement would be false. For the same reason `picSharp` may
49	not be wired to the *absolute* functor `PicSharp.presheaf`.
50	
51	## Main results
52	
53	* `picSharp` — the relative Picard functor `Pic^♯_{C/k}`.
54	* `divFunctor` — the relative-divisor functor `Scheme.DivFunctor C.hom` of
55	  `Picard/DivFunctorDef.lean` (Kleiman §3 Def. `df:div`, invertible-kernel
56	  quotient encoding).
57	* `PicScheme`, `representable`, `instPicSharpRepresentable` — the representing
58	  scheme and the natural bijection
59	  `(T ⟶ Pic_{C/k}) ≃ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)` it induces.
60	* `instPicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType`, `isSeparated` — `Pic_{C/k}` is locally
61	  of finite type and separated over `k` (Kleiman §4 Thm `th:main`(1): it is a
62	  disjoint union of open quasi-projective `k`-subschemes).
63	* `groupSchemeStructure` — `Pic_{C/k}` is a commutative `k`-group scheme, by
64	  Yoneda transport (`CommGrpObj.ofRepresentableBy`) of the abelian-group
65	  structure of `PicSharp.relPresheaf`.
66	* `abelMapWitness`, `abelMap`, `abelMap_app_mk` — the Abel map
67	  `Div_{C/k} ⟶ Pic^♯_{C/k}`, `[D] ↦ [O(D)] = -[ker q]` (Kleiman §3
68	  Def. `dfn:Abel`), assembled as `abelKernelNatTrans C ≫ picNeg C`.
69	* `smoothProperQuotient` — the Altman–Kleiman quotient lemma (Kleiman §4
70	  Lem. `lm:qt`), relative to the use-site hypothesis class
71	  `HasSmoothProperQuotient`.
72	
73	## Remaining obligations
74	
75	One statement in this file is still `sorry`: `instHasPicScheme`, the existence
76	of a scheme that represents `picSharp C` and is separated and locally of
77	finite type over `k`, given a rational point. Mathematically this is Kleiman
78	§4 Thm `th:main`(1) together with Cor `cor:algsch`, transported through §2
79	Thm 2.5. Everything else here — in particular representability of the chosen
80	scheme, its local finiteness, its separatedness, and its group-scheme
81	structure — is derived from that one existence statement.
82	
83	`smoothProperQuotient` is stated against an explicit hypothesis class rather
84	than proved outright, because the hypothesis list expressible here is weaker
85	than Kleiman §4 Lem. `lm:qt`: it omits quasi-projectivity of the representing
86	scheme `Y`, for which Mathlib has no vocabulary at the pinned revision.
87	Without that hypothesis the statement is false — a Hironaka-type free
88	`ℤ/2`-action on a smooth proper non-projective 3-fold gives a smooth proper
89	equivalence relation whose quotient étale sheaf is an algebraic space that is
90	not a scheme. The class must therefore be supplied at the use site, where

315	private theorem abelKernel_welldef {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))

321	  obtain ⟨f, hf⟩ := h
322	  exact Quotient.sound (PicSharp.relPicRel_of_iso
323	    ⟨(kernelCompMono x.q f.hom).symm ≪≫ Limits.kernelIsoOfEq hf⟩)

325	/-- **Kernel commutes with base change for a divisor family** (the mathematical
326	heart of Abel-map naturality).  For a test map `g : T ⟶ T'` and a divisor family
327	`x` over `T`, the ideal of the pulled-back family is the pullback of the ideal:
328	`ker((g_C^* x).q) ≅ g_C^*(ker x.q)`.  Proof: `(pullbackAlong g.unop x).q` is

453	/-! ## §3. The smooth-proper quotient lemma — Altman–Kleiman descent
454	
455	The structural lemma underlying Step 4 of Kleiman §4 Thm. `th:main`: given a
456	surjection `α : Z ⟶ P` of étale sheaves with `R := Z ×_P Z` representable,
457	`Z` representable **by a quasi-projective scheme**, and the first projection
458	`R ⟶ Z` smooth and proper, the quotient `P` is representable.
459	
460	The hypothesis list expressible here is strictly weaker than Kleiman §4 Lem
461	`lm:qt`: it lacks **quasi-projectivity of `Y`**, for which Mathlib has no
462	vocabulary at the pinned revision. Without it the statement is false: a
463	Hironaka-type free `ℤ/2`-action on a smooth proper non-projective 3-fold
464	gives a smooth proper equivalence relation satisfying hypotheses (1)–(4)
465	whose quotient étale sheaf is an algebraic space that is not a scheme. In
466	particular there is no global instance of `HasSmoothProperQuotient`; such an
467	instance would assert that every presheaf receiving any natural
468	transformation is representable.
469	
470	`HasSmoothProperQuotient α` is therefore an **explicit use-site hypothesis**:
471	the intended consumer (the FGA assembly, Step 4 of `th:main`) instantiates it
472	for the Abel-map slice `Z ⟶ P^{φ_0}_0`, where `Z` is a quasi-projective open
473	of `Div_{C/k}` and Altman–Kleiman descent genuinely applies. Supplying that
474	instance is part of the `instHasPicScheme` obligation, not a standalone
475	global fact.
476	
477	Blueprint reference: `lem:smooth_proper_quotient` (Kleiman §4 Lem. `lm:qt`). -/
478	
479	/-- Hypothesis class packaging the CONCLUSION of the Altman–Kleiman
480	smooth-proper quotient lemma for a specific étale-sheaf surjection `α`:
481	that the target presheaf is representable.
482	
483	There is deliberately no global instance: an unconditional one would be a
484	false statement (see the section header). The class is supplied at the use
485	site, where the Kleiman `lm:qt` hypotheses — including quasi-projectivity of
486	the representing scheme, which the `smoothProperQuotient` statement below
487	cannot express — actually hold.
488	
489	The class is kept as the blueprint-pinned record of the Altman–Kleiman
490	`lm:qt` interface. A route to `instHasPicScheme` that takes only finite
491	Galois quotients with an orbit-in-affine hypothesis sidesteps the
492	Hironaka-type counterexample above, and so needs neither this class nor
493	`smoothProperQuotient`. -/
494	class HasSmoothProperQuotient {k : Type u} [Field k]
495	    {Z P : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (u + 1)}
496	    (_α : Z ⟶ P) : Prop where
497	  is_representable : P.IsRepresentable
498	
499	/-- **The smooth-proper quotient lemma — Altman–Kleiman descent of an
500	étale-sheaf surjection** (Kleiman §4 Lem. `lm:qt`).
501	
502	Let `Z, P : (Sch/k)^op ⥤ Type (u+1)` be presheaves and `α : Z ⟶ P` a natural
503	transformation with: (1) `Z` representable by `Y`; (2) `R := Z ×_P Z`
504	representable by `R`; (3) the first projection `π : R ⟶ Y` smooth and proper;
505	(4) `α` an étale-local surjection (every `T`-point of `P` lifts along some
506	test morphism). Then, granting the use-site hypothesis
507	`[HasSmoothProperQuotient α]` (which additionally encodes Kleiman's
508	quasi-projectivity of `Y` — see the section header for why it cannot yet be
509	stated internally), `P` is representable.
510	
511	The Lean body extracts the conclusion from the hypothesis class; the
512	mathematical content (Altman–Kleiman effective-equivalence-relation descent
513	+ EGA IV 8.11.5) lives at the use site supplying the instance. -/
514	theorem smoothProperQuotient {k : Type u} [Field k]

# B3 — the rigid pushforward engine: statement layer and ℙ¹ reduction skeleton

This file pins milestone **B3** of the Picard-representability campaign
(`informal/pic-representability-campaign.md`), the engine
`pushforward_locallyFree_of_h1_vanishing`: for the constant curve
`C_A = C ×_k Spec A` over a finitely generated `k`-algebra `A` and an
invertible sheaf `L` on `C_A` with `h¹(C_t, L_t) = 0` at **every scheme
point** `t : Spec A`, the pushforward `q_* L` along `q : C_A ⟶ Spec A` is
locally free with fibre rank `h⁰(C_t, L_t) (= χ(L_t))`, and its formation
commutes with **arbitrary** ring maps `A → A'`.

Sources: Mumford, *Abelian Varieties*, II §5 (the two-term finite free
complex and "cohomology and base change"); EGA III 7.9.9; Hartshorne III
12.11; Kleiman, *The Picard scheme* (FGA Explained), §5 — B3 is the engine
behind Kleiman's flattening/openness arguments in the curve case.

## Statement audit (campaign checklist item 1 — BLOCKING; verdicts recorded here)

* **Quantifier — `h¹ = 0` at ALL scheme points** (`RigidPushforwardLocallyFree`,
  `RigidPushforwardBaseChange`): the hypothesis `∀ t : Spec A,
  q.FiberH1Vanishing L t` ranges over *all* points of the underlying space of
  `Spec A` (all primes), not only closed points.  For general noetherian `A`
  (noetherian ≠ Jacobson: e.g. a DVR, whose generic point is contained in no
  closed point's closure) the closed-point form is strictly weaker and the
  engine's conclusion FAILS if the hypothesis is checked at closed points
  only.  A finitely generated `k`-algebra *is* Jacobson, so on the pinned
  base the two forms happen to agree — but (i) the reduction uses h¹ upper
  semicontinuity, an engine we refuse to smuggle into the *statement*, and
  (ii) milestone B2 extends every consumer along filtered colimits and
  localizations, where the base is merely noetherian and Jacobson genuinely
  fails.  All campaign consumers (J1/J3 `h⁰ ≡ 1`, B4–B6) supply the
  hypothesis at all scheme points anyway.  VERDICT: pin at all scheme points.
* **Base change along ARBITRARY `A → A'` in the statement**
  (`RigidPushforwardBaseChange`): quantified over every commutative ring
  `A' : Type u` and every ring hom `φ : A →+* A'` — no finiteness, no
  flatness, no noetherian hypothesis on `A'`.  The comparison morphism is
  the canonical `pushforwardBaseChangeMap` (Stacks 02N4-style mate) of the
  *defining pullback square* of `q` along `Spec φ`, so the statement is
  well-formed with zero transport: the base-changed family is
  `pullback q (Spec.map φ)` — canonically (but not definitionally) isomorphic
  to `C ×_k Spec A'`; the comparison iso is postponed to the consumer layer
  (B2), keeping the pin transport-free.  VERDICT: arbitrary `A'`, arbitrary
  `φ`, canonical square, comparison map in the statement.
* **Two-step pin**: step 1 = rank-`χ` local freeness
  (`RigidPushforwardLocallyFree`) + base change
  (`RigidPushforwardBaseChange`); step 2 = the rank-one corollary
  (`pushforward_isLocallyTrivial_of_h1_vanishing`, proved from the gate).
  VERDICT: pinned as two separate `Prop`s consumed by one gate.
* **Rank = `χ(L_t)`** : under `h¹(L_t) = 0` we have `χ(L_t) = h⁰(L_t)`, and
  `h⁰` *is* expressible today (`Scheme.Hom.fiberH0`, the `κ(t)`-dimension of
  `Γ(C_t, L_t)`, matching `Scheme.hilbertFunction`'s convention), while the
  `χ`-ledger is milestone P3.  The rank is therefore pinned as
  `q.fiberH0 L t`; **P2/P3-interface TODO**: once the P2 cohomology kit and
  the P3 `χ`-ledger land, add the (definitionally compatible) reformulation
  `rank = χ(L_t) = deg L_t + 1 - g`.
* **Fibrewise `h¹` vocabulary** (P2 does not exist yet): the hypothesis is
  pinned in the weakest honest form the adelic lane can already express —
  existence of a 2-affine Čech cover (`AffineCoverMVSquare`, the lane's
  carrier) of the scheme-theoretic fibre on which the degree-1 Čech
  cokernel of `L_t` vanishes, i.e. the difference-of-restrictions map is
  surjective (`Scheme.Hom.FiberH1Vanishing`; carrier form
  `AffineCoverMVSquare.moduleH1Cok`, mirroring
  `AffineCoverMVSquare.H1Cok` of `RiemannRoch/Adelic/Cokernel.lean`).  On a
  separated scheme with an affine 2-cover, this Čech `H¹` computes sheaf
  `H¹` for quasi-coherent modules (Mayer–Vietoris/Leray; in-lane precedent
  `hModuleOne_linearEquiv_cechCohomology`), and any two such covers agree —
  cover-independence is exactly the **P2-interface TODO**, to be discharged
  Čech-to-Čech.  The ∃-form is chosen because it is *implied* by every
  future kit form, so the gate only gets easier to discharge.
* **The rank-one corollary's `DivFamily` leg** (Kleiman §5; campaign J2):
  `h⁰ ≡ 1, h¹ ≡ 0 ⟹ q_*L` invertible is pinned and proved from the gate
  below.  The continuation — the counit section `q^*q_*L ⟶ L` is fibrewise
  nonzero, hence a regular section on the integral fibres, hence cuts a
  canonical `DivFamily` — needs the counit/adjunction vocabulary on the
  `Div` side and the geometric integrality of fibres; it is recorded as the
  **J2-interface TODO** and deliberately NOT pinned here (its natural home
  is the J2 session, where the target `DivFamily` shape is fixed).

## Gate

`HasRigidPushforward C` is the campaign gate (`HasPicScheme` pattern): a
`Prop` class with **no instances anywhere**, carrying the two statement
`Prop`s quantified over all finitely generated `k`-algebras.  It is
discharged by the full B3 session (Mumford two-term complex route) and
deleted on discharge.  Everything else in this file is *proved*: the
extraction theorems, the rank-one corollary, and the ℙ¹ reduction skeleton
(the base-changed finite map `C_A ⟶ ℙ¹_A`, the pushforward factorization
`q_* = p_* ∘ π_*`, and the reduction of B3-for-`C_A` to a ℙ¹ engine plus a
named finite-pushforward transfer package).
-/

curve `C_A` to the ℙ¹ engine plus a *finite-pushforward transfer package*
along the finite map `π_A : C_A ⟶ ℙ¹_A` (`rigidPushforwardLocallyFree_of_p1`,

transfer hypotheses:

  `pushforward_finiteMapToP1BaseChange_isFinitePresentation`: the finite
  pushforward `(π_A)_* L` of an invertible module is finitely presented.
  The engine behind it is the general noetherian coherence criterion
  `Scheme.Modules.isFinitePresentation_of_finite_sections`: a quasi-coherent
  module on a locally noetherian scheme whose section modules over affine
  opens are finite is finitely presented.  The pushforward is quasi-coherent
  by Stacks 01XJ (`pushforward_isQuasicoherent`, proved in
  `Picard/QuotScheme.lean`), its sections over an affine `V` are
  `Γ(L, π_A⁻¹ V)` *definitionally*, and these are module-finite over
  `Γ(ℙ¹_A, V)` by composing the module-finiteness of the finite morphism
  `π_A` (Stacks 01WG) with the finiteness of the sections of the finitely
  presented `L` on the affine `π_A⁻¹ V` (Stacks 01PC,
  `finite_sections_preimage_of_isAffineHom`).  `A` is a finitely generated
  `k`-algebra, hence noetherian (Hilbert basis), hence `ℙ¹_A` is locally
  noetherian and finite section modules are finitely presented.

492	      (constMap C).hom c :=

486	/-- The structure ring map at the top open is the global-sections structure map
487	`constMap` of `Picard/SectionRingUniversal.lean`: the restriction along
488	`⊤ ≤ ⊤` is the identity (`map_id`, applied pointwise — `kToSection (op ⊤)` is
489	definitionally `constMap` followed by the restriction along `𝟙 (op ⊤)`). -/
490	lemma kToSection_top_apply (c : k) :
491	    (toModuleKSheaf.kToSection C (Opposite.op (⊤ : C.left.Opens))).hom c =
492	      (constMap C).hom c :=
493	  congrArg (fun g => CommRingCat.Hom.hom g ((constMap C).hom c))
494	    (C.left.presheaf.map_id (Opposite.op (⊤ : C.left.Opens)))

496	/-- **`Γ(C, 𝒪_C) = k` in `BaseSections` form**: the unconditional
497	field-of-constants theorem `globalSectionsAlgEquivBase`
498	(`Picard/SectionRingUniversal.lean`, `HasTrivialConstants` discharged
499	unconditionally via H⁰ flat base change) as a `k`-linear equivalence
500	`BaseSections C 𝒪 ⊤ ≃ₗ[k] k` — the `BaseSections` scalar path at `⊤` is the
501	`constMap` scalar path (`kToSection_top_apply`). -/
502	noncomputable def unitTopSectionsEquivBase [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] :
503	    BaseSections C (SheafOfModules.unit C.left.ringCatSheaf) (⊤ : C.left.Opens) ≃ₗ[k] k where
504	  toFun x := globalSectionsAlgEquivBase C (x : Γ(C.left, ⊤))
505	  invFun c := ((globalSectionsAlgEquivBase C).symm c : Γ(C.left, ⊤))
506	  map_add' x y := map_add (globalSectionsAlgEquivBase C) x y
507	  map_smul' c x := by
508	    have hb : baseRingMap C (⊤ : C.left.Opens) c = (constMap C).hom c :=
509	      kToSection_top_apply C c
510	    change globalSectionsAlgEquivBase C
511	        (baseRingMap C (⊤ : C.left.Opens) c • BaseSections.val x) =
512	      c • globalSectionsAlgEquivBase C (BaseSections.val x)
513	    rw [hb]
514	    exact (globalSectionsAlgEquivBase C).toLinearEquiv.map_smul c (BaseSections.val x)
515	  left_inv x := (globalSectionsAlgEquivBase C).symm_apply_apply x
516	  right_inv c := (globalSectionsAlgEquivBase C).apply_symm_apply c
517
